newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MOTOR CYCLING-MALAYSIA GRAND PRIX FUTURE IN DOUBT.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR CYCLING-MALAYSIA GRAND PRIX FUTURE IN DOUBT.

text.p: International organisers have warned Malaysia it will be dropped from the circuit completely if it fails to stage its world motorcycle grand prix in April as scheduled, the national Bernama news agency reported on Tuesday.

The Automobile Association of Malaysia (AAM), one of the local sponsors, said race organiser Dorna had threatened to cut Malaysia off the grand prix circuit if this year's race did not go ahead on April 13.
"I've got a letter from Dorna, saying this country will never be picked again for the race it if withdrew now," Bernama quoted AAM general manager Khir Anuar Mohamed as saying.

Malaysia's central Selangor state, which has hosted the event since 1991 at the Shah Alam race circuit, has said it does not plan to renew its contract for the 1997 race after disagreeing with certain conditions set by Dorna, Bernama said. Selangor hopes to rejoin the grand prix circuit in 1999.
Khir urged Selangor to reconsider its stance, saying the grand prix was important to Malaysia's tourism, with live television coverage of the event being beamed to around 150 countries.
"Our move now should be to get sponsors who are ready to fund the race," he said, adding that some eight million ringgit ($3.2 million) was needed.
Last year's race cost the Selangor government about six million ringgit.
